question: to the Commission Regina Doherty (PPE) Subject:

Can the Commission clarify whether current EU VAT legislation permits Ireland to apply a 0 % VAT rate to the purchase of a newly constructed home by a first-time buyer, where that property will be used as the purchaser’s principal private residence and, if a 0 %VAT rate cannot be targeted specifically at first-time buyers, whether Ireland could apply a 0 % or super-reduced VAT rate to a defined category of affordable owner-occupied housing, subject, for example, to a maximum property value, income threshold or requirement that the property remain the purchaser’s principal residence for a specified period?
What conditions would have to be satisfied for such a measure to qualify as the provision of housing ‘as part of a social policy’ for the purposes of the VAT Directive?
If a 0 % rate is not permissible, what is the lowest VAT rate Ireland could lawfully apply to such newly constructed homes under the current EU VAT framework?
